contexts.text: An age in the Word is ten years.
They live there (under Gehenna) for ages...
The greatest and least times are commonly distinguished in the Word into three or seven, and are called either days, weeks, months, years, or ages.
Some had remained there (in an infernal tun) for twenty ages.
An age = what is perpetual.

Hence was derived the fact that times were likened to these metals, and were called the Golden, Silver, Bronze, and Iron Ages... the Golden Age was the time of the Most Ancient Church... the Silver Age was the time of the Ancient Church, ... the Bronze Age was the time of the succeeding Church, to which there succeeded the Iron Age. DP 328:3.
The last time of the Church is signified by the third day, the third week, the third month, the third year, and by the third age, which are the same.
Days of an age = the Most Ancient Church. Illustrated. AC 4926:3.
When evil and falsity began to reign, or when after the Golden Age the Iron one began.
After vastations of many ages.
Hence the Ancients distinguished the times from the first to the last age of the world into the Golden, Silver, Copper, and Iron Ages, to which they added one of clay. (These ages described.)
Even to the desire of the hills of an age = to celestial mutual love, the hills of an age = what is of mutual love. Explained.
Mountains of eternity = good of love of the Most Ancient Church, hills of an age = good of mutual love of that Church; the former its internal, the latter its external. Illustrated.
Ye shall see them again no more for ever = falsities once put away are put away to eternity.
For ever = what is eternal. AC 9966:end. AC 10248. AC 10371. AC 10447.
(The times of the Golden Age described.) AC 10355:2. HH 252. DP 215. AR 211.
The reason why for ever = what is eternal is that by an age is meant duration even to the end... the same word also in the original tongue by which an age is expressed signifies eternity.

The reason an age is what is eternal is that an age, when said of the Church, signifies duration even to the end. Hence when it is said of Heaven, where there is no end, and when of the Lord, it signifies what is eternal. It is in general predicated of every Church, but especially of the Celestial Church. An age further signifies the world and life there; and also the life after the former one to eternity. (All these significations of an age fully illustrated.)
The times called the Silver Age described.
(The times called the Golden, Silver, Copper and Iron Ages described.)

I spoke with some one who had been in the Ancient Church... they were in a miserable state... they said they had been there for many ages, and that they were sometimes taken out to serve others for certain uses that were vile.
In the west towards the front dwelt those of that religion who had lived in the dark ages. LJ 61:6. SE 5317.
For ever and ever = to eternity. AR 60. AR 374. AR 520. AR 864. AE 33. AE 84. AE 468, Illustrated.
Marriage love was the love of loves with the Ancients who lived in the Golden, Silver, and Copper Ages. General article. CL 74 et seq.
(The people who had lived in the Golden Age visited.) Coro 37.
(The people who had lived in the Silver Age visited.)
They were from peoples in Asia.
(The people who had lived in the Copper Age visited.)
(Also those of the Iron Age.)
Oh the gross stupidity of the age! AE 481. Explained.
(Duration of vastation and of punishment for centuries.) SE 1497. SE 5098.
(Why the Ancients named the Ages after these metals.) AE 176.
(Why it is said for ever and ever, and not eternal.)
It is natural to say for ever and ever, but spiritual to say eternal.
For ever and ever = continually. Explained.
